title: VESPER Authorization — Grant, Capability, ContextFragment
description: IC-009 / IC-003. COC Part VII is a taxonomy of six levels with no evaluator: under it, shell.run('ls') and shell.run('rm -rf ~') are the same tool at the same level. This contract supplies the missing subject, argument sensitivity, delegation rule and taint ceiling that DF-AUTHORIZE evaluates. Authority: Part VII, RB-010, RB-011, RB-025, RB-028, DR-014, DR-020, T-002; REM-003, REM-004.

grant.description: THERE IS NO AMBIENT AUTHORITY. A subject holding no grant may act at L0 only (INV-AUTH-1). Default-deny is not a setting; it is the absence of any code path that produces a level without a grant.

subject_kind.description: REM-004 made the runtime a first-class subject of its own change control. INV-SELF-3: effective_level L5 with subject_kind 'runtime' is DENIED unconditionally -- including under a valid L5 grant and under break-glass.

delegable.description: INV-AUTH-2. Unattenuated INHERITANCE, not self-grant, is the real escalation path: SR-014 permits unbounded worker fan-out, so without attenuation a worker summarising a hostile web page holds its parent's L4.

issued_for_command_id.description: REQUIRED for L4/L5. One confirmation authorizes ONE action instance -- not a task, not a session, and never six workers' worth of external action.

allOf.$comment: INV-AUTH-2 -- L4/L5 are never delegable and always bind to one command instance.

capability.description: IC-003. declared_level MUST be a total FUNCTION over args (INV-AUTH-5). A capability registering a constant is refused at registration and fails CI-011 earlier.

args_schema.description: JSON Schema for this capability's arguments.

declared_level_rules.description: Ordered predicate -> level rules evaluated against args. minItems 2 makes a constant structurally unexpressible: at least one discriminating rule plus a default. Example for fs.write: path in GOVERNED_PATHS -> L5; path in workspace -> L2; default -> L4.

when.description: Predicate over args. 'default' permitted only as the final rule.

reconcilable.description: REM-012 s2. A tool with no read-only 'did this happen?' probe declares false and MUST escalate to the user rather than retry. This is the case that silently produces duplicates, so it is handled by declaration.

state_changing.description: Drives the taint ceiling: a context containing retrieved_external caps state-changing capabilities at L1 (INV-AUTH-3).

allOf.$comment: INV-EXT-1 -- irreversible capabilities are at least L4 and must be reconcilable or escalate.

contextFragment.description: The taint carrier. INV-AUTH-3: taint propagates through summarisation, embedding and cache reuse -- a summary of tainted content is tainted. This is the sentence an implementation omits, because summarisation naturally produces a clean-looking new string; CI-012 exists to catch its omission.

trust_class.description: allowed_level: system L5, owner L5, verified_local L4, retrieved_local L3, model_generated L2, retrieved_external L1. Unknown or absent provenance is treated as retrieved_external -- the most restrictive class.

derived_from.description: Fragment ids this was summarised, embedded or cached from. trust_class MUST equal min(derived_from.trust_class) -- a cache entry with no trust_class is a CACHE MISS, not a trusted hit.

context_role.description: INV-AUTH-6: a fragment with trust_class 'retrieved_external' may NEVER appear in a 'planner' context. The two-context research pattern is architectural: the high-authority planner never ingests raw external content; a low-authority extraction context does and returns only schema-validated structured data.

allOf.$comment: INV-AUTH-6 stated structurally rather than as a runtime check alone.
